value.body: A real estate analyst studies how land and buildings are used, priced and developed in a city. Property consultancies, developers, and real-estate funds hire them. A typical day involves collecting project and price data, reading development control rules, and putting together market notes or site feasibility reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Plan, B.Arch, BBA or an economics degree

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, GIS software, master plans and development control regulations

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join the research or valuation-support team of a property consultancy or developer as an analyst or associate. A planning background helps with zoning, land-use and master-plan questions; financial modelling is often learned on the job.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading master plans and development control regulations
Market data collection and analysis in Excel

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior analyst, research manager, land acquisition or valuation roles.
Work volume follows the property cycle, so hiring can rise and fall with the market.
Valuation work for banks or courts may need separate registration as a valuer.
